entries.lesson_title: Definition of the Unit Step Function
entries.lesson_core_move: State the value-based definition of the unit step function and interpret it as the basic continuous-time on-off signal used to build shifted, delayed, and rectangular-pulse signal descriptions.

sections.section_title: Introduction to Definition of the Unit Step Function
sections.learning_goal: Define $u(t)$ as a binary, continuous-time switching signal and state its values on each side of the switching instant.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach the course convention $u(t)=0$ for $t<0$ and $u(t)=1$ for $t>0$, then explicitly state the chosen convention at $t=0$ for this topic line.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Introduce the simplest base case with one test instant $t=2$ and one instant $t=-1$ to show off versus on states.
paragraph_plan: Open with a short interpretation: $u(t)$ is the continuous-time switch that controls whether output is gated off or on.
State the value rule for negative time: for $t<0$, the switch is off and $u(t)=0$.
State the value rule for nonnegative time: for $t>0$, the switch is on and $u(t)=1$.
State the course boundary choice at $t=0$ and warn learners to keep it consistent within this lesson.
Preview why this definition is the foundation for shifted and delayed switch forms and rectangular-pulse construction.

sections.handoff_notes: Keep direct instruction minimal and explicit about the $t<0 and t>0 regions before moving to substitutions$.

sections.section_title: Evaluating the Unit Step Before and After the Switch
sections.learning_goal: Apply the definition pointwise for times strictly before and strictly after the switch.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Compute $u(t)$ at sample points from different regions, such as $u(-4)$, $u(-0.1)$, $u(3)$, and $u(10)$.
distractor_plan: Include responses that flip sign regions, such as treating negative times as on and positive times as off.
Include off-by-one mistakes using $t>0$ versus $t\ge0$ boundaries in nonboundary points.
Include value slips that return $u(t)=\pm 1$.
Include distractors that confuse switch timing with pulse midpoint values.
Include a response using undefined or error notation for ordinary evaluation points.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Evaluate $u(-4)$ and $u(3)$ with the definition from the tutorial.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Map each query time to the correct region and return the correct on/off value.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This extends the base definition by evaluating multiple numeric points without any graph dependence.
solution_step_plan: Classify each time as strictly less than zero or strictly greater than zero.
Apply the region rule for each class.
State the final scalar value for each query.
practice_variation_axes: Multiple negative query points
Multiple positive query points
Single-step pointwise substitution

sections.handoff_notes: Keep examples strictly symbolic so question generation can mirror with different time values.

sections.section_title: Evaluating the Unit Step at the Switching Time
sections.learning_goal: Handle the switching instant consistently by applying the lesson’s convention for $t=0$.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Under this lesson convention, determine $u(0)$ and compare it with $u(-0.01)$ and $u(0.01)$.
distractor_plan: Include options that set $u(0)=0$ or $u(0)=0.5$ to catch convention confusion.
Include options that apply one-sided values to exactly $t=0$.
Include sign inversion errors where on/off labels are swapped.
Include choices with mixed correct and incorrect boundary symbols in one option.
Include options that repeat $u(-0.01)$ or $u(0.01)$ without a true boundary value.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Evaluate $u(0)$ and decide whether it differs from both one-sided limits.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Separate interior-case evaluation from boundary-case evaluation and report the boundary value explicitly.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Adds the one meaningful wrinkle of a boundary-time case after pure left/right substitution.
solution_step_plan: State the previously learned off/on rules.
Identify $t=0$ as the boundary-time case.
Apply the topic convention for $u(0)$.
Optionally compare with $u(0^-)$ and $u(0^+)$ for contrast.
practice_variation_axes: Boundary value vs left/right neighbor values
Explicit convention checks
Detecting and correcting silent assumption that boundary equals left side

sections.handoff_notes: Keep conventions explicit so downstream question generation does not drift between $u(0)=1$ and $u(0)=0$ policies.

sections.section_title: Reading the Unit Step Function from a Time-Axis Graph
sections.learning_goal: Infer $u(t)$ values from a graph while preserving the same off/on convention.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A time-axis graph of a binary step with one jump between 0 and 1 at a switching instant, with clear axis labels and a marker at the switch.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Keep the graph minimal and uncluttered so learners read value regions without decorative cues.

question_policy.practice_question_model: From the graph, identify $u(-2)$, $u(0)$, and the value interval where the signal is on.
distractor_plan: Include distractors that shift the switch instant incorrectly.
Include distractors that reverse on/off interpretation when reading the same graph.
Include distractors that assume continuous transition rather than a jump.
Include options that mix graph regions and output values.
Include a distractor that confuses axis units and reads time labels as value levels.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Read the graph and compute $u(t)$ for three selected times, including the switch instant.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Translate graph features into pointwise values by checking where each query lies relative to the switch.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Introduces one visual representation while preserving the same scalar-lookup logic from symbolic examples.
solution_step_plan: Read the switch location from the graph.
Classify each query time as left or right of that location.
Assign the corresponding binary value based on region.
For the switch instant, apply the lesson convention used in the tutorial.
practice_variation_axes: Different query times on the same graph
Changing graph with same off/on heights but different switch time
Boundary instant interpretation from visual data

sections.handoff_notes: Use a single-step visual style in the generated graph prompt that can be mutated across practice instances by changing switch position only.

sections.section_title: Recognizing the Unit Step as the Basic Continuous-Time Switching Signal
sections.learning_goal: Identify and interpret $u(t)$ as the operator that turns a continuous-time signal on for the right side of a switch.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Choose the correct interpretation of $u(t)x(t)$ when $x(t)=t^2$.
distractor_plan: Include distractors that describe no switching effect on $x(t)$.
Include distractors that reverse the active side (left-hand instead of right-hand support).
Include distractors that turn on at negative time by default.
Include distractors that confuse with a delayed expression $u(t- t_0) x(t)$.
Include distractors that treat the step as phase offset instead of amplitude gating.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Rewrite and interpret the piecewise signal defined by $x(t)u(t)$ with $x(t)=t^2$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Explain that the product suppresses output for $t<0$ and passes $t^2$ for $t\ge0$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Shifts from direct value lookup to structural interpretation that prepares shifted and delayed switch forms.
solution_step_plan: Write the product as a piecewise expression using the known values of $u(t)$.
State the two regions explicitly: off region and on region.
Verify the resulting on-off behavior against the definition.
practice_variation_axes: Different smooth test functions $x(t)$
Recognition of region boundaries in product form
Selecting the correct off-state for the left region

sections.handoff_notes: Do not introduce shifted arguments yet; keep focus on the canonical $u(t)$ and its gating interpretation only.

entries.lesson_title: Unit Step as an On-Off Switch
entries.lesson_core_move: Interpret x(t)u(t) as using the unit step as an on-off switch that suppresses a continuous-time signal before t = 0 and passes it afterward, supporting construction of started, delayed, and pulsed signals with unit steps.

sections.section_title: Introduction to Unit Step as an On-Off Switch
sections.learning_goal: Introduce the exact gate interpretation of multiplication by $u(t)$ and map it to the two regions that control whether $x(t)u(t)$ is active or suppressed.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: Not needed; this section is fully symbolic with value-based case analysis.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach learners to evaluate $u(t)$ as a switch so $y(t)=x(t)u(t)$ equals $0$ for $t<0$ and equals the active signal after the switch point.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use $x(t)=1$ so the switch action is transparent in $y(t)=u(t)$.
paragraph_plan: Start by recalling the value rule for $u(t)$ and state that a switched product becomes a regionwise product rule.
Show the generic decomposition $y(t)=x(t)u(t)=\begin{cases}0, & t<0\x(t), & t\ge 0\end{cases}$ using exact notation.
Emphasize interpretation: the factor $u(t)$ suppresses the signal before $0$ and allows it through after $0$, with the same $x(t)$ form unchanged in the active region.

sections.handoff_notes: Do not introduce any delayed or shifted step terms in this tutorial; reserve $u(t- t_0)$ and subtraction constructions for later topics.

sections.section_title: Evaluating x(t)u(t) Before t = 0
sections.learning_goal: Train learners to identify the pre-switch region and compute $x(t)u(t)$ there as an explicit zero output.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No graph is required because the switch check is purely symbolic by sign of t.

question_policy.practice_question_model: For $y(t)=x(t)u(t)$ with $x(t)=t^2+1$, evaluate $y(-4)$.
distractor_plan: Substitute into $x(t)$ but forget to apply $u(-4)=0$.
Apply the wrong region and evaluate with $t>0$ logic.
Return the full expression $x(-4)$ instead of $0$.
Use an incorrect switch value and output a nonzero constant.
Conflate the case with $t=0$ and apply boundary convention.
Apply $u(-4)=1$ by mirroring the nonnegative region.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Evaluate $y(t)=(2-t)u(t)$ at $t=-1$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Show that $u(-1)=0$ forces $y(-1)=0$ regardless of the active formula.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Uses the same switch concept but moves from general definition to a concrete sample in the blocked region.
solution_step_plan: Find the switch value at $t=-1$: $u(-1)=0$.
Compute $u(-1)x(-1)$ by explicit substitution.
State the final output using the multiplication rule: $y(-1)=0$.
practice_variation_axes: Replace $x(t)$ with trigonometric or polynomial expressions.
Use different negative sample points.
Keep the switch at $0$ while changing $x(t)$ scale and sign.

sections.handoff_notes: Keep all distractors around the same algebraic complexity so this remains a clean controlled step before varying templates.

sections.section_title: Evaluating x(t)u(t) After t = 0
sections.learning_goal: Train learners to evaluate switched outputs in the on region where $u(t)=1$ and the result matches the active formula $x(t)$.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: Image use not needed for sample-point symbolic evaluation in $t>0$.

question_policy.practice_question_model: For $y(t)=x(t)u(t)$ with $x(t)=3t-4$, evaluate $y(2)$.
distractor_plan: Multiply by $0$ in the active region.
Use pre-switch logic and return $0$.
Compute $x(2)$ but lose track of sign changes.
Treat $u(t)$ as undefined and skip multiplication.
Return a normalized or halved value not matching $x(2)$.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Evaluate $y(t)=(3t+1)u(t)$ at $t=2$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Keeps the same procedure but applies the same rule in the on region.
solution_step_plan: Find the switch value at $t=2$: $u(2)=1$.
Compute $u(2)x(2)$ explicitly.
State final numeric output and connect it to unchanged transmission of $x(t)$ after zero.
practice_variation_axes: Different positive sample points in the on region.
Different $x(t)$ formulas with constants, polynomials, and fractions.
Change only the arithmetic complexity while preserving the on-region logic.

sections.handoff_notes: Frame this as the mirror of the prior section so learners see the same switch rule with opposite output.

sections.section_title: Writing the On-Off Output of x(t)u(t) in Piecewise Form
sections.learning_goal: Convert a switched signal from product form to full piecewise representation so the on-off behavior is explicit for all time regions.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No diagram needed; this is a symbolic region split into two cases.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Write $y(t)= (5-2t)u(t)$ in piecewise form.
distractor_plan: Keep only $y(t)=5-2t$ and omit the zero branch.
Write the wrong inequality orientation for the branches.
Use $<0$ and $>0$ boundaries swapped.
Insert $x(t)$ into both branches identically.
Include an incorrect switch value at $t=0$ in the inactive region.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Express $y(t)=(4t+1)u(t)$ as an explicit piecewise function of $t$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Create a piecewise rule with a zero branch before the switch and $4t+1$ at and after the switch point.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from evaluating at sample points to writing the full regionwise definition used for later delayed and windowed forms.
solution_step_plan: Start from the general gate identity for $x(t)u(t)$.
Set the inactive branch for $t<0$ and active branch for $t\ge 0$.
Substitute $x(t)=4t+1$ only in the active branch.
Verify that the output is continuous with the product interpretation.
practice_variation_axes: Different $x(t)$ expressions (constant, polynomial, exponential-like symbolic forms).
Use alternative boundary convention in distractor crafting only (e.g., $t>0$ vs $t\ge 0$) to test convention clarity.)
Ask for full piecewise output instead of point evaluation to reinforce structure.

sections.handoff_notes: Keep boundary handling explicit and match the course convention used in prior unit-step lesson for consistency.

entries.lesson_core_move: Translate shifted unit step functions into exact switch-on times on the continuous-time axis so they can be used to start, delay, and construct signals compactly.

sections.section_title: Introduction to Shifted Unit Step Functions
sections.learning_goal: Introduce how time shifts in the argument of $u(\cdot)$ set the switch-on time and distinguish delays from advances.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No image required; this is a pure symbolic timing-rule tutorial.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach that $u(t)$ switches from 0 to 1 at $t=0$, and that $u(t-T)$, $u(t+T)$, and $u(t-t_0)$ shift that switch to the solve-for-$t$ instant of the shifted expression.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Start from $u(t)$, where the switch-on time is exactly $t=0$.
paragraph_plan: State the base definition: $u(t)=0$ for $t<0$ and $u(t)=1$ for $t\ge 0$.
Show the shifted form $u(t-T)$ and solve the switch condition $t-T=0$ to get a single switch-on time $t=T$.
Contrast with $u(t+T)$ by solving $t+T=0$, giving switch-on time $t=-T$, and interpret this as an advance when $T>0$.
Introduce parameterized form $u(t-t_0)$ and map the generic rule: switch-on at $t=t_0$.
Summarize that future examples only vary coefficient sign and location, not the base rule.

sections.handoff_notes: The next sections should stay tied to this single rule: set the inside of the unit-step argument to zero and read that time as the switching instant.

sections.section_title: Finding the Switch-On Time from u(t - T)
sections.learning_goal: Determine the switch-on time from a delayed unit step and keep the sign convention stable.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No image needed; identify timing from algebraic argument.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given $u(t-\alpha)$ with numeric $\alpha$, ask for the switch-on time and one distractor by sign change.
distractor_plan: Offer $t=0$ as a distractor from the unshifted unit step rule.
Offer $t=-T$ as the advance-style distractor with swapped sign interpretation.
Offer $t=T/2$ as a scaling distractor.
Offer no switch time as a distractor for learners who miss that steps are not one-sided zero always.
Offer an expression in $1/T$ that confuses arithmetic with geometry.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Find the switch-on time of $y(t)=u(t-3)$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Solve $t-3=0$ and report the switch-on time as $t=3$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This is the first concrete worked example using the tutorial base rule on a positive delay.
solution_step_plan: Write the switch condition from the argument: $t-3=0$.
Solve for $t$ and get $t=3$.
State the value profile: $y(t)=0$ for $t<3$, $y(t)=1$ for $t\ge 3$.
practice_variation_axes: Change the numeric delay constant while preserving the $u(t-T)$ form.
Vary whether the value asked is switch-on time or active interval start.
Add a context phrase that changes wording but keeps the same algebraic transformation.

sections.handoff_notes: Keep this step strictly one-step and one-step-only: determine the single point where the expression changes from 0 to 1.

sections.section_title: Finding the Switch-On Time from u(t + T)
sections.learning_goal: Determine switch-on time for the advanced-shift form $u(t+T)$ and avoid sign reversal errors.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No image required; this step reinforces the same algebraic rule in a sign-reversed form.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given $u(t+\alpha)$ with numeric $\alpha$, ask for the switch-on time and identify the sign rule used.
distractor_plan: Offer $t=+\alpha$ to catch learners who copy the previous delay rule.
Offer $t=0$ to catch learners who forget the shift.
Offer a late time such as $-\alpha/2$ as arithmetic confusion distractor.
Offer a reversed inequality interpretation where switching is thought to happen at $t<-\alpha$ as a directional distractor.
Offer a no-switch option for a valid step-like function.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Find the switch-on time of $y(t)=u(t+2)$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Use $t+2=0 \Rightarrow t=-2$ to locate the switch-on time, then confirm the function turns on at negative time.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Controlled sign-flip extension: reuse the same solve-for-$t$ rule from the previous section, but now with $+$ inside the argument.
solution_step_plan: Set the inside equal to zero: $t+2=0$.
Solve for $t$ to get $t=-2$.
Conclude the timing rule: function is 0 before $-2$, and 1 for $t\ge -2$.
practice_variation_axes: Change the shift parameter value while keeping a plus sign.
Ask for the pre/post value regions as a second item.
Swap wording between ‘turn-on time’ and ‘switch time’ for transfer.

sections.handoff_notes: Make the + sign pitfall explicit in examples and distractors; this is where many learners confuse with the previous delay rule.

sections.section_title: Finding the Switch-On Time from u(t - t0)
sections.learning_goal: Apply the same solve-for-zero rule when the shift symbol is a named parameter $t_0$.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No image needed; all timing is determined symbolically from the argument root.

question_policy.practice_question_model: For a generic form $u(t-t_0)$ choose the corresponding switch-on time from given numeric values of $t_0$, including negative values.
distractor_plan: Offer a distractor that substitutes $t_0$ into numerator/denominator patterns.
Offer $-t_0$ to catch sign-reflection errors with parameter names.
Offer $t_0+1$ to test arithmetic overreach.
Offer the previous section's sign-reversed result.
Offer no-switch outcome for non-numeric $t_0$ to detect symbolic confusion.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: If $y(t)=u(t-t_0)$ and $t_0=-1$, find the switch-on time.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Solve $t-t_0=0$ then substitute $t_0=-1$ to conclude switch-on at $t=-1$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This step generalizes the numeric rule to a parameterized delay so the same operation works on symbols.
solution_step_plan: Write the switching equation $t-t_0=0$.
Rearrange to get $t=t_0$.
Substitute $t_0=-1$ to report the switch at $t=-1$.
practice_variation_axes: Vary numeric $t_0$ (positive, zero, negative) while keeping form identical.
Ask for final step-function profile after finding $t_0$ as a second part.
Include distractors that invert parameter assignment.

sections.handoff_notes: Keep parameter logic explicit: the delay amount and switch-on time are equal when argument is $t-t_0$.

sections.section_title: Placing Shifted Unit Steps on the Time Axis
sections.learning_goal: Position shifted steps on a time axis by converting arguments to switch-on times and ordering multiple steps quickly.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A clean time-axis chart showing three labeled vertical step points for arguments like $u(t-4)$, $u(t+1)$, and $u(t-t0)$ with unknown t0 left as a marker.
visual_elements: vertical markers at computed switch-on times
labels for each shifted step name
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Image should encode only axis positions and labels; no additional grid complexity.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given three shifted step forms, ask for the ordering of switch-on times (or earliest/latest) with one correct ordering and 4 plausible wrong orderings.
distractor_plan: Swap one pair of times by sign error in one term.
Use one incorrect ordering that keeps values but inverts $-\infty$ to $+\infty$ direction.
Include the unshifted ordering from $u(t)$ as a control distractor.
Invert all signs to produce a mirror-image axis order.
Use equal-time ordering that ignores distinct constants.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Order the switch-on times of $y_1(t)=u(t-2)$, $y_2(t)=u(t+1)$, and $y_3(t)=u(t-5)$ from earliest to latest.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Compute switch-on times $2$, $-1$, $5$ and return ordering $-1 < 2 < 5$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Adds multiple shifted steps in one step so students transfer the single-form rule to comparative placement on the axis.
solution_step_plan: Convert each argument equation to zero: $t-2=0$, $t+1=0$, $t-5=0$.
Solve each switch-on time: $2$, $-1$, and $5$.
Sort times from smallest to largest and connect each time to the corresponding expression.
Attach a quick verbal check: the $u(t+1)$ term must switch first because it is advanced.
practice_variation_axes: Vary the set of shifted expressions and include one negative constant with one positive parameterized form.
Shift emphasis between identifying one earliest switch and full ranking.
Add a distractor item with $u(t+\beta)$ where $\beta>0$ to reinforce naming conventions.

sections.handoff_notes: Use a simple axis diagram for the tutorial step only; keep follow-up questions textual/ numeric because the skill is comparison of solved switch times.

entries.lesson_title: Starting a Signal with a Unit Step
entries.lesson_core_move: Convert a zero-before-start continuous-time signal from piecewise form into a step-gated expression by multiplying the active formula by the unit step that turns on at the start time.

sections.section_title: Introduction to Starting a Signal with a Unit Step
sections.learning_goal: Map a zero-before-start piecewise signal to a single step-gated formula by introducing the unit step as an on/off switch on a given interval.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No visual support needed. The target move is symbolic and best taught with algebraic expressions only.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach learners to write a one-interval, start-time-gated signal as an active formula times $u(t-t_0)$ where the step introduces the exact switch time.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Start with a step at the origin: convert $x(t)=0$ for $t<0$ and $x(t)=f(t)$ for $t\ge0$ into $x(t)=f(t)u(t)$.
paragraph_plan: Name the target move as converting a two-part definition into a compact step-gated form.
Define the active interval and inactive interval in words, using the start time language $t<t_0$ and $t\ge t_0$.
Introduce the shift rule: a signal is turned on at $t=t_0$ by multiplying with $u(t-t_0)$.
Walk a concrete $f(t)$-based example at $t_0=0$ from piecewise form to gate form.
Summarize boundary handling guidance and emphasize that only the switch in the step determines where the active branch appears.

sections.handoff_notes: Build immediately into a controlled worked example in the next section by applying the same conversion rule to a non-constant active formula that starts at 0.

sections.section_title: Starting an Active Formula at t = 0
sections.learning_goal: Convert a two-case signal with zero before 0 to a step-gated formula using $u(t)$, preserving the exact active expression for $t \ge 0$.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No image required. Signal transition is conveyed by step shift in algebraic notation.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Convert $x(t)=0$ for $t<0$ and $x(t)=2t+1$ for $t>=0$ into an equivalent unit-step expression.
distractor_plan: Use $u(t-1)$ or another shifted step instead of $u(t)$, misplacing the start time.
Drop the active branch's argument shift and write $2t+1$ unchanged by the gate.
Reverse branch order and write the active and inactive formulas swapped.
Write a step-gated sum of two formulas or add an unnecessary subtraction term.
Omit the boundary condition and treat $t=0$ as either active or inactive inconsistently.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Write a unit-step form for $x(t)=0$ for $t<0$ and $x(t)=2t+1$ for $t>=0$.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce one concise step-gated expression: $x(t)=(2t+1)u(t)$.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from tutorial base case to a concrete symbolic active formula, still with switch at the origin.
solution_step_plan: Identify the active branch interval $t>=0$.
Choose the gate factor $u(t)$ for a start at zero.
Multiply the active branch formula by the gate and keep inactive part implicit as zero.
Optionally rewrite as $x(t)=(2t+1)u(t)$ and check the $t < 0 region evaluates to 0$.
practice_variation_axes: Switch same gate time 0, change active polynomial formula.
Use constant, linear, or quadratic active branch while keeping one-sided switch at 0.

sections.handoff_notes: Keep the active branch expression untouched; only add the gating factor from the start-time pattern.

sections.section_title: Starting an Active Formula After t = 0
sections.learning_goal: Convert a piecewise signal that begins at a positive start time into the correct shifted step-gated expression.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No visual needed. Shifted start time is shown with $u(t-t_0)$ notation only.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Convert $x(t)=0$ for $t<t_1$ and $x(t)=e^{-t}$ for $t>=t_1$, with $t_1=3$, into unit-step form.
distractor_plan: Use $u(t)$ instead of $u(t-3)$, missing the delayed switch.
Shift the argument on the formula and the step inconsistently, e.g., $e^{-(t-3)}u(t)$.
Leave active branch as $e^{-t}$ while multiplying by the correct shift and then evaluate incorrect boundary behavior.
Add constants such as $u(3-t)$, which switches at the wrong side.
Omit domain check around $t=t_1$ and treat all t identically.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Convert $x(t)=0$ for $t<2$ and $x(t)=2\,e^{-t}$ for $t>=2$ to a unit-step expression.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce $x(t)=2e^{-t}u(t-2)$ and validate the two intervals.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Introduces delayed start time and reinforces that only the step argument changes while the active formula remains unshifted in this pattern.
solution_step_plan: Read the switch time from the inactive-active boundary: start at $t=2$.
Write the gate as $u(t-2)$ for a delayed activation.
Multiply the same active formula $2e^{-t}$ by $u(t-2)$.
Verify that for $t<2$, the output is 0, and for $t>=2$, the output is $2e^{-t}$.
practice_variation_axes: Positive delay values $t_1>0$.
Different delayed active formulas (constant, exponential, polynomial).
Use $t_1$ as either integer or fractional delays for transfer of the shift rule.

sections.handoff_notes: Do not shift the active formula's independent variable unless the follow-on topic explicitly asks for delayed argument changes.

sections.section_title: Starting an Active Formula Before t = 0
sections.learning_goal: Convert a piecewise signal with negative start time into a step-gated expression and track a gate that turns on before the origin.

image_policy.image_generation_notes: No image needed. Use shifted gate $u(t-t_0)$ with $t_0<0$ as text.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Write a unit-step expression for $x(t)=0$ for $t<-1$ and $x(t)=\sin(t)$ for $t>=-1$.
distractor_plan: Use $u(t+1)$ which flips the switch direction.
